Summary: This bill would require the Department of Transportation (DOT) to establish a trade-in program, subject to appropriation, and provide vouchers for class one and class two bicycles with electric assist, at reduced cost or no cost, to a food delivery worker who trades in an eligible device. DOT would be required to conduct outreach regarding the program and to report on the implementation of the program.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the establishment of a trade-in program concerning powered bicycles

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subchapter 3 of chapter 1 of title 19 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 19-199.2 to read as follows:
§ 19-199.2 Trade-in program for powered bicycles. a. Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
Class one bicycle with electric assist. The term “class one bicycle with electric assist” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision (a) of section 102-c of the vehicle and traffic law. 
Class two bicycle with electric assist. The term “class two bicycle with electric assist” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision (b) of section 102-c of the vehicle and traffic law.
Class three bicycle with electric assist. The term “class three bicycle with electric assist” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision (c) of section 102-c of the vehicle and traffic law. 
Designated citywide languages. The term “designated citywide languages” has the same meaning as set forth in section 23-1101. 
Eligible device. The term “eligible device” means: (i) a class three bicycle with electric assist; (ii) a class one bicycle with electric assist or a class two bicycle with electric assist that does not meet, or for which the storage battery does not meet, the requirements for distribution, sale, lease, or rental pursuant to section 20-610; or (iii) a vehicle with 2 or 3 wheels that is equipped with operable pedals, and that has an electric motor with a power output of less than 750 watts that is capable of providing assistance at speeds between 25 miles per hour and 28 miles per hour.
Food delivery worker. The term “food delivery worker” has the same meaning as set forth in section 20-563. 
Participant. The term “participant” means a food delivery worker who meets the eligibility requirements for the program established pursuant to this section, as set forth in rules promulgated by the commissioner.
Powered bicycle. The term “powered bicycle” means a bicycle with electric assist, as such term is defined in section 102-c of the vehicle and traffic law.
Powered bicycle business. The term “powered bicycle business” means a business that sells, leases, or rents powered bicycles.
b. 1. Subject to appropriation, the commissioner, in consultation with the commissioner of consumer and worker protection and the head of any other agency deemed relevant by the commissioner, shall establish a trade-in program to provide access to a powered bicycle that is a class one bicycle with electric assist or a class two bicycle with electric assist that meets the requirements for distribution, sale, lease, or rental pursuant to section 20-610, at reduced cost or no cost, to a participant who trades in an eligible device. The commissioner shall consult with delivery worker advocacy organizations and powered bicycle businesses regarding the establishment of such program, including but not limited to the date, time, and location of events hosted pursuant to paragraph 4 of this subdivision, and outreach conducted pursuant to subdivision d of this section. 
2. Such program shall provide to a participant who trades in an eligible device any one of the following, as determined by the commissioner:
(a) A voucher that such participant may use toward the cost of purchasing a class one bicycle with electric assist or a class two bicycle with electric assist from a powered bicycle business;
(b) A voucher that such participant may use toward the cost of the lease or rental of a class one bicycle with electric assist or a class two bicycle with electric assist from a powered bicycle business; or
(c) A means, other than a voucher to use toward to the cost of purchasing, leasing, or renting a class one bicycle with electric assist or a class two bicycle with electric assist from a powered bicycle business, for such participant to obtain access to a class one bicycle with electric assist or a class two bicycle with electric assist, as determined by the commissioner.
3. A participant who trades in an eligible device shall be limited to receiving no more than 1 voucher pursuant to subparagraphs (a) and (b) of paragraph 2 of this subdivision, or access to no more than 1 class one bicycle with electric assist or class two bicycle with electric assist pursuant to subparagraph (c) of paragraph 2 of this subdivision.
4. The commissioner shall host at least 2 events in each borough each calendar year to administer the program established pursuant to this subdivision.
c. Rulemaking. The commissioner shall promulgate rules for the program established pursuant to subdivision b of this section. Such rules shall set forth:
1. Eligibility requirements for a food delivery worker to participate in such program; 
2. Eligibility requirements for powered bicycle businesses that accept vouchers described in subparagraph (a) or (b) of paragraph 2 of subdivision b of this section; and
3. An application process for participants.
d. Outreach. The commissioner, in consultation with the commissioner of consumer and worker protection and the head of any agency deemed relevant by the commissioner, shall conduct a public outreach campaign regarding the program established pursuant to subdivision b of this section. Such campaign shall include in-person and virtual outreach in the designated citywide languages and any additional languages as determined by the commissioner.
e. Reporting. The commissioner shall make available the following information on the department’s website, and shall update such information no less than quarterly, and as frequently as the commissioner determines is necessary to ensure the accuracy of such information:
1. The total monetary value of any vouchers provided pursuant to subparagraph (a) or (b) of paragraph 2 of subdivision b of this section, or the total monetary value of access to a class one bicycle with electric assist or a class two bicycle with electric assist provided to a participant who trades in an eligible device pursuant to subparagraph (c) of paragraph 2 of subdivision b of this section.
2. The average monetary value of any vouchers provided pursuant to subparagraph (a) or (b) of paragraph 2 of subdivision b of this section, or the average monetary value of access to a class one bicycle with electric assist or a class two bicycle with electric assist provided to a participant who trades in an eligible device pursuant to subparagraph (c) of paragraph 2 of subdivision b of this section;  
3. The number of powered bicycle businesses who accepted vouchers provided pursuant to subparagraph (a) or (b) of paragraph 2 of subdivision b of this section;
4. A description of any method utilized to dispose of an eligible device a participant trades in through the program established pursuant to subdivision b of this section; 
5. The number of participants in such program;
6. A description of the events hosted pursuant to paragraph 4 of subdivision b of this section;
7. The number of vouchers provided to participants pursuant to subparagraph (a) or (b) of paragraph 2 of subdivision b of this section; and
8. The number of participants who sought to trade in an eligible device pursuant to the program established by this section, but who were not able to trade in such a device due to lack of sufficient funding.
§ 2. This local law takes effect 545 days after it becomes law.
